newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes steady amid talk of deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes steady amid talk of deals.

text.p: A steady U.S. West Coast crude market continued to be perturbed out of its pre-holiday torpor Wednesday by rumblings of deals both on Alaskan North Slope (ANS) and on grades within California, traders said.
To be sure, some traders had already called it a day by the local noon hour (2000 GMT), but those still working their phones were saying some deals were getting done.

British Petroleum, one the biggest ANS sellers into the California market, reported closing a 100,000 barrel deal at the relatively pricey level of $1.75 under January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for delivery by the end of the month.

The hastiness of the delivery schedule, the small sub-cargo volume involved in the deal, plus the fact the putatative buyer denied having done the deal -- made it difficult for buyers to view the market as truly stronger.

The last confirmed cargo deal was on Tuesday when BP sold a 600,000 cargo to BHP for Honululu delivery in December, though the $1.95 under January WTI price level reported by BP appeared to be the subject of some disagreement. Some buyers said they were still bidding at $2.20 under.
Deals on San Joaquin Valley heavy from the Kern River region were meanwhile heard done at postings, or $17 a barrel.

While buyers and sellers of San Joaquin Valley crude could not be confirmed, some traders said Mobil Corp, faced with a downed coker unit at its Torrance refinery in the Los Angeles region, has recently been a seller of the grade.
They said Mobil is long by as much as 100,000 barrels of the heavy crude, which is said to be well suited for running through its coking unit.
Mobil has declined to comment on when the refinery might be back up, but some traders have said this week they expect the unit to be back up by sometime next week.

The U.S. Thankgiving holiday on Thursday will leave the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) closed on Thursday and Friday, and some West Coast traders said they would not bother to show for work until next Monday.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
